arc: From arriving in a running world to making its first elements: a point gains a body, an address, a relation, a record and a face. Connected faces become generated forms. Separate rooms then ask what the engine supplies, how a column separates profile from sampling, and what borrowed letter outlines can become. The closing halls consider a chosen tolerance and a composition made with known tools.

halls.title: Once, then again
halls.storyboard: The student encounters the existing museum counter, then reads and runs its smallest complete study: create a Label3D in _ready, attach it, and update its text with the engine frame total in _process. Move the reading to _ready to hold one value while the engine continues. The tutorial prints one complete program, explains every necessary connection and names the exact move for the once-only experiment; camera and player are supplied by Day Zero. Native tests execute the printed code without production-script completion and reject omitted label creation or attachment. Carry execution timing into Point One; keep arrival and borrowed time in final.md.
learns: _ready: initialize when the node is ready
supplied: Day Zero running project, camera, light and player
halls.review_note: 5 October author correction: smallest complete working code must be visible and tested. This is a reduced learner study of the existing counter, not edits hidden within its production implementation.
halls.storyboard_short: Meet museum counter. Print/run complete label + frame-reading study. Create and attach in _ready; update in _process; compare once-only reading. Supply Day Zero camera/player only. Assert exact printed code; missing creation/attachment must fail. Carry execution timing.

halls.title: Give a point a body
halls.storyboard: Encounter the corridor's absent, visible and solid points, then build one small point from scratch in point.gd on an empty PointStudy Node3D inside the prepared project. _ready creates a StaticBody3D, sphere mesh and collider. A named centre and radius control position and both boundaries. Change each value; hide the surface or disable collision to separate seeing from contact. The complete code is printed once and executed by native assertions, including the edited states. Carry this actual program into Coordinates. Day Zero supplies room, camera, light and player, not the point.
learns: Create and attach a visible surface
halls.carries: The exact point.gd construction continued in Coordinates
supplied: Day Zero room, camera, light and player
An empty PointStudy Node3D at floor level
halls.review_note: Printed small construction and exact edits have native behavioural evidence. It is a learner study of the existing corridor, with no museum-runtime changes. See doc/book/iterations/2026-10-05-points-built-and-carried/index.html.
halls.storyboard_short: Meet corridor points. New point.gd on empty PointStudy in prepared project. _ready builds StaticBody3D + mesh + collider; shared centre/radius. Test position, size, visibility and collision independently. Print complete code once; assert exact script/edits. Carry same program to Coordinates. Supply room/view/player only.

halls.title: A point we can move
halls.storyboard: Meet the museum's held point, then continue the exact point.gd made in Point One. Preserve centre, radius and mesh/collider construction; change the body to XRToolsPickable and supply its pickup settings before adding it to the scene. Create a Label3D and update WORLD from global_position and LOCAL through PointStudy.to_local. Grip, carry and release the same authored construction; disable pickup to isolate permission; move the station to distinguish frames. Test the printed program and its exact predecessor composition in native Godot using the real XR library and synthetic controller. Carry a movable, readable point into Lines. Day Zero supplies configured hands/library; distance is deferred.
learns: Local and world position in named frames
halls.carries: Point One's authored body construction with pickup and a live coordinate readout
supplied: Day Zero room, camera, light and configured XR hands
halls.review_note: The readout is now created in the printed code. Native evidence tests overlap/grab/release and frame conversion; it does not prove hardware input or headset experience. Lines now continues this exact tested construction and preserves the readout.
halls.storyboard_short: Continue exact Point One point.gd. Preserve shape construction; StaticBody3D becomes XRToolsPickable. Set pickup configuration before tree entry. Create Label3D; per-frame WORLD=global_position, LOCAL=PointStudy.to_local. Test permission, hold/release, frame change. Supply XR hands/library. Native assertions + exact predecessor composition. Carry point; defer distance.

halls.title: Put two points in relation
halls.storyboard: Move familiar geometry and pickup settings into PointBody._init; make A and B with .new; keep positions/readout/relation in the lesson. Convert both ends to local coordinates; subtract, measure and draw.
brings: The tested pickable point from Coordinates
halls.carries: PointBody class, two independent pickable instances, coordinate readout and live segment. Trace reuses the class unchanged.
supplied: Prepared unit-scale museum room, camera/light and configured XR hands/library
halls.review_note: The complete printed script extracts the tested Coordinates construction into point_body.gd and creates two instances. The class construction is checked against the predecessor. Each point owns its mesh and collider; native XR pickup, resource independence and line relations are verified.
halls.storyboard_short: Extract familiar point into PointBody. _init builds mesh/collider/settings; XRToolsPickable supplies pickup. Two .new instances, own resources. Lesson owns placement/readout/segment. Explain class vs instance; test independent movement/resources, release, local relation and pairs. Carry class unchanged to Trace.

halls.title: Keep the positions
halls.storyboard: Move the point already built in Point One and made pickable in Coordinates. Trace keeps selected local positions in an array, uses a distance condition to admit a sample, and loops over neighbours to join them. Predict which motion is retained and try another threshold. Release the point to save its positions and existing drawing through the supplied archive. Bring that work into the next museum hall; Grid will receive the sculpture instead of asking for another gesture.
brings: The verified Lines program, unchanged PointBody class and LineSkin renderer.
learns: Saving the drawing for the next hall
halls.carries: The saved segment sculpture and ordered local positions in user://ada_student_trace.scn. Metres, PointStudy-local frame, no timestamps; a later valid release replaces the save.
supplied: The existing Endless Museum hall, player and XRTools; fully printed TraceArchive supplies packing and loading. PointBody and LineSkin return unchanged.
halls.review_note: 6 October author correction: bring the actual saved drawing into the next museum hall. Native source-bound tests and actual-hall checks pass; headset and human learning not tested.
halls.storyboard_short: BRING same PointBody + LineSkin. RECORD local metre positions; Array, append/index, distance IF, neighbour FOR. RELEASE saves positions + existing segment sculpture via supplied TraceArchive. CHECK pause/threshold/order/geometry + cross-process load. CARRY actual saved work to Grid; no timestamps.

halls.title: Give that trace addresses
halls.storyboard: Meet the drawing made in Trace as a sculpture in the Grid hall. Load its saved geometry and local position record; make neither a new sphere nor another gesture. Keep the original pink while a separate copy receives rounded XYZ addresses. Predict a corner, compare two pitches and flatten only the copy to test what the rule changes. The original remains available for another use, including choosing three corners in Triangle.
brings: The actual drawing saved on release in Trace, its local position record and the unchanged LineSkin renderer.
learns: Reusing a drawing as a sculpture
Changing a copy while keeping the original
halls.carries: Original saved sculpture and positions, independently owned derived segments and integer XYZ addresses. The drawing file and original record survive every comparison.
supplied: The existing Endless Museum Grid hall, light and player; the same fully printed TraceArchive supplies loading. Desktop ui_accept changes pitch; the initial grid_step can be edited for VR.
halls.review_note: 6 October author correction: bring the actual saved drawing into the next museum hall. Native source-bound tests and actual-hall checks pass; headset and human learning not tested.
halls.storyboard_short: BRING saved Trace sculpture + positions. LOAD in same museum project; no new point/gesture/geometry recipe. KEEP pink source. COPY with independent resources; round XYZ/pitch to Vector3i; place green via earned LineSkin. TEST source/file/geometry unchanged, absent save, .25/.50, flat-Y. CARRY original to Triangle.

halls.title: A boundary becomes a face
halls.storyboard: Bring the original saved Trace positions through Grid. Choose three entries, reuse PointBody as temporary handles, and connect them with one ordered triangular face. Move a corner, reverse the front, and collapse the triangle to see why a guard is needed. The archive stays intact. Carry positions and a face recipe into the first enclosure.
learns: A closed boundary and a face
A guard for a collapsed triangle
halls.carries: A face made from chosen positions
halls.review_note: Use non-collinear positions. Defer arbitrary polygon filling.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH Three selected array entries; A closed boundary and a face; Clockwise vertex order; A guard for a collapsed triangle. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Carry positions and a face recipe into the first enclosure.

halls.title: Connect faces around a space
halls.storyboard: Reload the same three selected Trace positions and add an apex behind their plane. Store four positions once and address them with four face-index triples. Move the shared apex and see three faces change together; distinguish a closed visible surface from a collider. Carry the position/connectivity separation and FaceBody into Cube.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH Shared vertices; A list of face-index triples; Tetrahedron connectivity; Surface enclosure versus collision. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Carry the position/connectivity separation and FaceBody into Cube.

halls.title: Keep the corners, change the connections
halls.storyboard: Build CubeBody from eight shared corners and twelve triangles using the previous face renderer. Compare two independent instances with different front-face diagonals. Deform a corner, then move the whole node, distinguishing a construction edit from a placement. Keep the reusable cube for later composition, Transformation and Arrays.
halls.carries: Edit a mesh without confusing it with object motion
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH A reusable CubeBody class; Shared corner data; Two triangles per square side; Connectivity versus object position. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Keep the reusable cube for later composition, Transformation and Arrays.

halls.title: A rule can make the positions
halls.storyboard: Generate an octahedron position list with a named function: positive and negative multiples of three axes. Supply the face recipe and render two independent returned lists at different radii. Call it again, modify only one result and explain the broken symmetry. Carry parameters, typed return values and the distinction between a rule and its output.
halls.review_note: The engine library and seven-form choir move to Godot. Columns takes the profile-and-rings follow-up; preserve the other secondary works here. Resolution, proportion and aesthetic judgement remain different decisions.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH Functions and typed return values; Parameters and arguments; Symmetry as a construction rule; Independent generated results. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Carry parameters, typed return values and the distinction between a rule and its output.

halls.title: The sphere in your hand
halls.storyboard: Return to PointBody and expose its actual SphereMesh as a member. Extend the class so held time decreases rings and radial segments, release pauses, re-grab continues and reset restores. Compare independent spheres and rings-only versus segments-only variants. Keep radius, visual identity and spherical collision fixed; stop at one ring and four segments. Carry controllable construction into Columns and later abilities.
brings: Existing PointBody construction and pickup behaviour
learns: A mesh resource and its parameters
halls.carries: A familiar sphere with an interaction that changes its resolution; a reusable route toward further abilities.
supplied: Existing Endless Museum room, player and XR library
Mesh library and seven-form choir as comparison specimens
halls.review_note: Author-selected object, not implemented new museum controls. Bind the small learner study host and retain its SphereMesh reference explicitly. Use rings >= 1 and radial_segments >= 4; test the complete later PointBody continuation without rewriting earlier evidence.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH Extending PointBody; A mesh resource and its parameters; Held and released states; Elapsed-time steps and lower bounds. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Carry controllable construction into Columns and later abilities.

halls.title: One outline, several bodies
halls.storyboard: Use a radius profile and two loops to generate stacked ring positions. Compare the same profile and height at 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16 sides with a supplied circle sampler and surface stitcher. Then change silhouette and height separately. Carry independent construction parameters and the profile/placement distinction into borrowed letter outlines.
learns: A profile as a radius list
Nested loops over rings and sides
Comparing one variable at a time
halls.carries: A column rule with separable shape, height and sampling inputs
supplied: Museum specimens and their curved-section builder
halls.review_note: The museum has fixed specimens, not live editing knobs. The reduced radius-list study uses straight intervals and ArrayMesh; do not call it a built-in PrimitiveMesh or equate more entries with smoothing. Agree where the learner’s edited column belongs in the museum.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH A profile as a radius list; Nested loops over rings and sides; Independent height and resolution; Comparing one variable at a time. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. halls.title: Borrowed outlines
halls.storyboard: Borrow the existing glyph sweep and its declared font to carry an O through five parallel placements. Separate the supplied outline, including its hole, from width, depth and sideways travel. Reverse the travel and try C while preserving the source. This produces a visible hollow mesh with a sill, not an assumed walk-through collider; keep font triangulation and arbitrary curved-path frames supplied or deferred.
brings: Profile and sampling are different inputs
A function can return geometry data
Supplied construction is not a guaranteed use
learns: A supplied outline with a hole
halls.carries: A borrowed profile with an explicit construction choice and use limitation
supplied: Font and six tested form recipes
halls.review_note: Choose a bounded learner edit host. The O sill is not a level doorway and the vessel has no bottom. Do not promise arbitrary glyph morphing, general path framing, accessible passage or a general topology lesson. Standalone atlas camera controls are not museum controls.

halls.title: Decide what is sufficient
halls.storyboard: Reuse circle samples and LineSkin to measure a closed polygon. Sum every neighbour edge including the last-to-first edge, compare with the finite TAU-based circumference reference, and increase sides until the stated metre tolerance is met or the sample budget is spent. Test tighter tolerances and an unattainable request. Carry an honest stopping criterion rather than a promise to reach infinity.
learns: A while loop with a stopping rule
halls.carries: A stated tolerance or visible purpose
halls.review_note: The sampler is supplied; full trigonometric construction is not assumed here.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH A closed neighbour loop; Error in a stated unit; A while loop with a stopping rule; A finite work budget. KEEP museum host; printed owned geometry; declare supplied helpers. TEST native + variant + deliberate fault. CARRY Carry an honest stopping criterion rather than a promise to reach infinity.

halls.title: Compose with what we have
halls.storyboard: Compose with two instances of the learned CubeBody and the familiar pickable PointBody. Change their placements without changing construction data; make a second arrangement and reconstruct it from saved script values. Use known constructors, arrays and a loop, leaving scale and rotation to Transformation. The reflective text carries the wider question of what making geometry is meant to give us.
halls.carries: A small arrangement that can change
halls.review_note: The critical discussion of geometric desire retains its own room; no new syntax is needed to finish.
halls.storyboard_short: TEACH Composition with known classes; Independent instances; Placement versus construction; Reusing a learned capability.
